final_rationale: The verdict does not change because no genuinely new admissible evidence was provided. The Actor response is a reframing of the same record and includes concessions that confirm the original concern: the exposed use case is not excluded, approved risk acceptance is absent, and 6% rollout, rollback, and monitoring do not cure the model-card weakness under the stated policy. That narrower framing is important for proportionality because it reduces overstatement risk, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats. The caveat here is not a minor disclosure note; it is an unresolved compliance condition that the policy makes mandatory before certification when the affected segment remains exposed. On the available admissible evidence, certification remains noncompliant.
remaining_concerns: The affected small-business onboarding use case remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort.
No completed, reviewed, and approved risk-acceptance record in the admissible record covers the exposed segment and its long-context onboarding limitation.
The policy text states that rollout controls and monitoring mitigate the model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or approved risk acceptance exists.
Explicit disclosure of the residual limitation reduces overclaim risk but does not satisfy the unmet policy predicate for certification.
